name: Paste event (read what the person pastes)
plain: Gives the page the clipboard contents, but only when the person presses paste inside the page.
meaning: A paste is consent for that one read: the site gets text, HTML or files the person chose to paste. It cannot peek at the clipboard at other times, which blocks silent snooping.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt (needs a click, tap or keypress)
access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Fires in the focused frame only
steps: Person presses Ctrl or Cmd+V (or the context menu Paste)
Page reads clipboardData: text, html, files

limits.headline: Can get what you paste, but only when you press paste on its page
limits.user_action: You press Ctrl+V, Cmd+V, or use Paste from the menu on the page
can: Receive text, HTML or files that you paste
Fill in a form field or an editor with it
cannot: See your clipboard when you did not paste
See what you pasted on other pages or apps
Get more than the one paste you did
limits.reach_label: One paste, when you press it

story.what_it_is: The page gets what you paste, but only when you press paste on it.

marketing.name: Clipboard events
marketing.pitch: Describes the paste event that gives pages the clipboard content when the person pastes into them.

story.for_you: You paste into a page with Ctrl+V or a right click and the content appears. Pasting counts as your yes for that one time. The page cannot peek at your clipboard at other times.
story.for_makers: Makers let people paste screenshots, tables and links into editors, chats and forms. They can also clean up pasted content or paste formatted text and images safely.

use_cases.example: A chat app lets you paste a screenshot from your clipboard right into the message box.
A document editor pastes a copied web table and keeps its columns.
A design tool turns a pasted image or SVG into a layer on the canvas.
A level editor or modding site lets you paste a map code into a box and loads it.
A site may block pasting into password or code fields, which annoys people with password managers.
A form tool records whether you pasted an email or typed it, as one more signal about bots.

technical_bounds: Only fires on a user paste in the focused document; scripts cannot trigger it with dispatchEvent for real data
Types readable: text/plain, text/html, text/uri-list and files (images, documents)
Pasted HTML is the browser sanitized form, not raw source from the source app
No permission prompt (the keystroke is the consent)
Pasted files expose name, size, type, lastModified; no path

legit_uses: Paste images into chat or docs
abuse: Capturing a sensitive clipboard after social engineering to press paste

history.change: paste event with clipboardData files for images
